sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Lakshman Singh,Ajay Sengar Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Saurabh Srivastava,J.
1.
Heard Sri Ajay Sengar, learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. Although notice has been issued to the opposite party no.2 and the same has been served, which is apparent from the office report, but till today none appeared on behalf of the opposite party no.2.

No counter affidavit has been preferred on behalf of the State as well as on behalf of opposite party no.2.
3.

The applicant, through the present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. have invoked the inherent jurisdiction of this Court with the prayer that the proceedings of Complaint Case No.2062 Western India C. Brnads Pvt. Ltd. vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94646456/
1 of 2000 (State of U.P. Versus Babu Lal Gupta & Another), under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 2/2000, P.S. Kotra Bazar, District Jalaun, pending before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jalaun at Orai be quashed.

sentences.text: 4. It is the case of the applicant that the opposite party no.2 filed a false and frivolous complaint case in District Jalaun against the applicant, whereupon only considering the statements of complainant and witnesses recorded under Section 200 and 202 Cr.P.C., learned Judicial Magistrate, Jalaun at Orai vide its order dated 07.09.2000, summoned the applicant without complying the mandatory provisions of Section 202 (1) Cr.P.C., since the applicant is resident of other districts.

5. Sri Ajay Sengar, learned counsel for the applicant, at the very outset, submitted that the summoning order, which has been put under challenge through the instant application is in non-compliance of Section 202 (1) of Cr.P.C., wherein it has been mentioned that if the summoning order has to be issued beyond the territorial jurisdiction of the concerned magistrate, the mandatory provision for inquiry is to be directed first and then after receiving the report, the summoning order may be issued.

6. From the perusal of the pleadings available on the record as well as the summoning order, it is crystal clear that without complying provision of Section 202 (1) of Cr.P.C. the concerned magistrate directly issued the summoning order against the applicant, who is residing at Gujarat.

7. However, learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the prayer as made in the instant application and rebutted the stand taken up by the learned counsel for the applicant but did not dispute the provisions of Section 202 (1) of Cr.P.C.
8.

In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, it is crystal clear that the concerned magistrate while presiding over its territorial jurisdiction, without complying the provision contained in Section 202 (1) of Cr.P.C. passed the summoning order and as such the summoning order dated 07.09.2000 is hereby set aside.
9.

However, it is made clear that learned Chief Judicial Magistrate/ concerned court will be at liberty to proceed afresh after extending credence to Section 202 (1) Cr.P.C. and ensure the compliance of the same as provided for issuing summoning orders beyond territorial jurisdiction of the concerned magistrate.
10. The Application U/S 482 is disposed of.
Order Date :- 22.5.2024
